jobs.title: Product Manager, Growth & Developer Experience, Remote Job
jobs.description: About Keycard At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku. The role We're hiring a Product Manager to own how teams evaluate Keycard, and the developer experience they meet when they do. Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Every customer starts with an evaluation, and today a field engineer runs each one by hand: setup, first credential exchange, integration questions. Your job is to turn that walkthrough into product, so an evaluation can run well without us in the room. You'll define what a successful evaluation looks like for an agent-identity product, instrument the journey so we can see where evaluators stall, then work with engineering to fix the worst spots. Sometimes the fix is a feature, more often it's a better quickstart, a template repo, an error message that says what to do next, or a docs page that assumed too much context. Expect to spend real time with the people running evaluations: watching onboarding sessions, sitting in on field-engineering walkthroughs, reading support threads, and finding out why a team went quiet mid-eval. What you'll do • Own the evaluation journey end to end, from first touch through first credential exchange to a production decision, including how each stage is defined and measured. • Set the evaluation milestones and metrics that product, engineering, and go-to-market all report against. • Own the developer experience an evaluation runs on: SDK quickstarts, CLI onboarding, console setup, docs, and template repos. • Drive time-to-first-credential-exchange down, and be the voice of developer ergonomics in engineering's API and CLI design discussions. • Turn what field engineering does by hand into self-guided paths: eval guides, reference architectures, in-product guidance. Run experiments and cut the ones that don't work. • Work with DevRel and marketing on how evaluations start, and with sales and field engineering on when a self-guided eval needs a human in the room. What we're looking for • You've been a PM on a developer product where evaluation and adoption were your numbers (dev tools, infrastructure, API platforms, or security). • Technical enough to be credible with engineers. You can read an SDK quickstart and see where a developer would bounce, follow an API design discussion, and pull your own numbers in SQL or an analytics tool. • You have taste in developer experience. You can articulate why one CLI feels good and another doesn't, and you notice error messages, defaults, and docs structure the way a designer notices spacing. • You build with AI tools yourself and follow the agent ecosystem closely enough to have real opinions about it. • You start from instrumentation. If the data you need doesn't exist, you get it added before forming theories about where evaluations drop off. • Comfortable in a category with no playbook. Agent identity is new, and a lot of this job is deciding which questions are worth answering. • You write clearly. Much of this role's output is docs, problem statements, and experiment readouts that other people act on. Strong candidates may also have • An engineering background before product; you've shipped code and understand what you're asking engineers to do. • Experience productizing a high-touch motion: turning field playbooks, POC guides, or solutions-engineering work into product. • Familiarity with identity/auth concepts (OAuth, OIDC, token exchange, delegation) or agent protocols (MCP, A2A). • Experience

jobs.title: Senior Technical Product Manager, Collection Management
jobs.description: At Dragos, the mission is personal. The systems we protect deliver the water you drink, power your home, and keep the hospitals your community depends on running. Those critical infrastructure systems that power our civilization around the world are under attack every day by adversaries. When those systems fail, people are immediately at risk. We are the global leader in xOT cybersecurity, combining technology, threat intelligence, and expert services. The people here chose this work because they understand what is at stake. Here, you will find a remote-first mission-driven team across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and APAC built on authenticity, transparency, and trust. If safeguarding the systems that protect your family, friends, and community is the kind of work that matters to you, you are in the right place. About the Role: Dragos is seeking a senior-level Technical Product Manager to own Collection Management, the shared function that every Dragos collection method depends on. Collection is how the Dragos Platform reaches an environment: sensors for passive traffic, agents on endpoints, active discovery and interrogation of devices, and integrations that pull from third-party systems. This role owns how collection methods are registered, kept healthy and updated, and tasked with work, and how their results come back into the platform. You will also own the contract all methods share. You will partner closely with the Product Managers and Engineering teams behind each method as well as Customer Experience (CX) to make sure a task or a result behaves the same way no matter which method handles it. Most of your customers are the other teams building the platform, so the work is coordination and technical product ownership more than external customer discovery. Responsibilities: • Define and own the product strategy and roadmap for Collection Management, covering inventory and registration, lifecycle and updates, health and connectivity, and the path results take into the platform. • Define the common collection contract (registration and pairing, health, updates, configuration and content, and tasking) and the security around it. • Define how work is dispatched to methods and how status, retries, and results return, including an audit trail of every action taken externally. • Define how collection methods are updated and receive content, moving from per-version packages to methods pulling what they need. • Define how entitlements apply to collection tasks. • Set requirements for secure credential handling. • Own requirements for ingest, including normalization of data to OCSF and the process for approving schema changes. • Work with constituent teams to establish and keep ownership boundaries clear: what should happen to a device, how it gets there, and how results resolve to an asset. • Partner with Product Managers and customer-facing teams (CX, Support, Sales Engineering) to gather real deployment conditions such as firewalls, proxies, certificates, and segmented networks, and validate designs against them. • Join customer conversations when a deployment issue or design question needs it. • Make prioritization and trade-off decisions across constituent teams, and communicate requirements to Engineering with a clear business rationale. • Define, track, and improve KPIs such as connectivity, deployment success, update adoption, and task completion rates. • Partner with Product Marketing, Support, and CX on documentation, launch plans. Qualifications: • 5+ years of Product Management experience, including experience owning a platform, infrastructure, or shared-service product that other teams build on. • Strong technical fluency with agent or collector architectures: registration, fleet inventory, health monitoring, update and staging mechanisms, and remote task execution. • Working knowledge of secure communications and identity, including TLS and mTLS, certificate lifecycle management, gRPC or similar RPC frame

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Product Operations
jobs.description: We Help the World Be Everyday Ready™ Today's threatscape is relentless. So are we. At Cyderes, we build practical Identity & Access Management (IAM), Exposure Management, and risk programs, helping organizations stop active threats fast with Managed Detection & Response (MDR) that integrates with existing tools. Powering it all is Meridian, our entity fabric that connects identities, assets, and access into one trusted reality. Augmented by AI and driven by experienced operators, our tireless global team arms organizations with the people, platforms, and perspectives they need to conquer whatever tomorrow throws their way. Great Place to Work® Certified™ About the Role: The Senior Product Manager, Product Operations is a product manager whose products are the internal systems that carry customer needs into Product: how escalations, detection tuning and hygiene checks for MDR customers, roadmap requests, and enhancement tickets are raised, prioritized, answered, and fed into the roadmap. You also define the product-side workflow for critical event response, and you lead company-wide programs to decommission infrastructure, platforms, and applications. This role is a critical role connecting the Product organization to Service delivery, the SOC, Customer Success, and Support who are your key partners and users while Engineering builds with you. You succeed when each process has a clear owner, a written workflow, and measures that show whether it works, and when what you learn from customer requests shows up in product priorities. Who you are You are a product manager first. You treat an internal process as a product: you find who uses it, what is failing for them, what a better version looks like, and how you will measure whether it got better. You write clear requirements, prioritize competing requests, and say no with evidence. You lead without authority. Escalation reviews and decommission programs depend on people in other teams, so you earn cooperation with clear plans, honest status, and follow-through. You use data to show what is working, you can specify and prioritize automation with Engineering, and you are not expected to write production code. Responsibilities: Customer escalations • Own the escalation process as a product: intake, severity levels, ownership, and handoffs between customer-facing teams, Product, and Engineering. • Turn escalation data into product insight by tracking volume, age, and root causes, and bring recurring causes into roadmap decisions. Critical event response • Define the product-side process for critical events, meaning failures or incidents that affect service delivery: how they are declared, who owns them, and how work is handed to Engineering. • Manage each critical event from the product side by coordinating Product's response, keeping stakeholders informed, and tracking follow-up actions to completion. • Run post-event reviews and carry root causes and lessons learned into roadmap priorities. Detection tuning and hygiene for MDR customers • Own one workflow for MDR customers that covers both detection tuning requests and customer hygiene checks. • Define intake standards, prioritization criteria, and turnaround targets for tuning requests. • Define how hygiene checks are monitored, reported, and acted on, including what happens when a check fails. • Track volume and outcomes, flag recurring requests that should become product capabilities, decide which checks to automate, and report customer health trends to product leadership. Enhancement ticket automation • Own the process and automation roadmap for enhancement tickets, from intake through routing and status updates. • Write requirements, prioritize the automation backlog, and define success measures with Engineering. Roadmap requests • Own the intake process and tooling for roadmap requests, with one view of requests grouped by customer and theme. • Give product managers evidence on what is being asked and why, and report decisions
